questions.explanation: CSDM stands for Common Service Data Model. It is ServiceNow's best-practice framework for modeling and managing the data within the CMDB to support the full lifecycle of services.

questions.question: You are creating a new form and want to add a field where the user can select a date and a time. What field type should you use?
answers: Date
Time
Date/Time
Timer
feedbacks: Incorrect: The 'Date' field type allows for selecting a date only, not a time.
Incorrect: The 'Time' field type allows for selecting a time only, not a date.
Correct: The 'Date/Time' field type provides a calendar and a time selector for the user to pick a specific date and time.
Incorrect: The 'Timer' field type is for tracking durations, not for selecting a point in time.
questions.explanation: When you need to capture a specific point in time, including both the date and the time of day, the correct field type to use is 'Date/Time'. This will provide the user with a user-friendly calendar picker and a time selection dropdown on the form.

questions.question: What is the function of a reference qualifier?
answers: It restricts the choices available for a reference field.
It automatically qualifies a user for a specific role based on their department.
It adds a quality score to a knowledge article.
It checks the qualifications of a CI before it can be used in a change request.
feedbacks: Correct: A reference qualifier is a filter that is applied to a reference field, limiting the records that a user can select.
Incorrect: This is not the function of a reference qualifier.
Incorrect: This is not the function of a reference qualifier.
Incorrect: This is not the function of a reference qualifier.
questions.explanation: Reference qualifiers are a powerful tool for improving data quality and the user experience. For example, on the Incident form, the 'Configuration Item' field is a reference field. You could add a reference qualifier to it that only shows CIs that are owned by the caller's department, making it much easier for the user to select the correct CI.

questions.question: Which of the following would you use to define a new table and its columns?
answers: Form Designer
Tables & Columns Module
A Database View
A Record Producer
feedbacks: Incorrect: Form Designer is for arranging the layout of a form for an existing table.
Correct: The 'Tables & Columns' module (or 'System Definition > Tables') is the primary interface for creating new tables and adding columns (fields) to them.
Incorrect: A database view is for joining existing tables for reporting, not for creating new tables.
Incorrect: A Record Producer is for creating records in a table, not for defining the table itself.
questions.explanation: The definition of the database structure—its tables and columns—is managed in the 'Tables & Columns' module. Here, an administrator can create a new table from scratch or by extending an existing one, and then add all the necessary fields (columns) by specifying their label, name, and data type.

questions.question: A user wants to be automatically subscribed to any knowledge article they create, so they are notified of any comments or changes. How can this be achieved?
answers: The user must manually subscribe to each article after they create it.
An administrator can create a Business Rule that subscribes the author upon article creation.
This functionality is not available in ServiceNow.
The user can set this in their main notification preferences.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is inefficient and can be automated.
Correct: A simple 'after' insert business rule on the Knowledge [kb_knowledge] table can be created to automatically add the author to the subscription list for that article.
Incorrect: This is a common requirement and can be easily automated.
Incorrect: This specific, conditional subscription is not a general notification preference; it requires a targeted automation.
questions.explanation: This is a great example of a simple but effective automation that can be built with a Business Rule. An administrator would create an 'after' business rule on the Knowledge [kb_knowledge] table that runs on 'insert'. The script would be very simple, using GlideRecord to create a new record in the subscription table (`kb_m2m_user_subscription`) linking the new article's sys_id to the author's sys_id.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about ACLs (Access Control Lists)?
answers: If a user has the 'admin' role, they will bypass all ACL rules.
ACLs can only be applied to tables, not to individual fields.
ACLs are client-side scripts that run in the user's browser.
If a user fails a table-level 'read' ACL, they can still see fields if they pass a field-level 'read' ACL.
feedbacks: Correct: By default, the 'admin' role has special privileges that allow it to pass all ACL checks. This is a key feature of the admin role.
Incorrect: ACLs can be applied at the table level (e.g., incident) or at the field level (e.g., incident.short_description).
Incorrect: ACLs are server-side rules that are evaluated at the database level.
Incorrect: If a user fails the table-level ACL, they are denied access to the entire record and its fields, regardless of any field-level rules.
questions.explanation: The 'admin' role in ServiceNow is designed to be a 'superuser' role for system administration. A key part of its power is that it bypasses standard data security rules, including ACLs. This allows an administrator to view and troubleshoot any record in the system, but it also means the role should be granted with extreme care.

questions.question: Which feature would you use to create a report that can be shared with users who do not have a ServiceNow license?
answers: Publishing the report
Scheduling the report
Exporting the report to PDF
Adding the report to a dashboard.
feedbacks: Correct: When you 'Publish' a report, ServiceNow generates a public URL. Anyone with this URL can view the report without logging in.
Incorrect: Scheduling sends the report via email to specific users or groups, who would typically need a license to interact further.
Incorrect: While this creates a shareable file, the 'Publish' feature provides a live, dynamic link.
Incorrect: Access to dashboards requires a user to log in to ServiceNow.
questions.explanation: The 'Publish' feature is designed specifically for sharing report data with an external audience. When an administrator publishes a report, they get a unique URL that can be embedded in other websites or sent via email. This provides a view of the report data to non-licensed users. It is important to remember that this makes the data public, so it should be used with care.

questions.question: What is a 'Client Script' in ServiceNow?
answers: A script that runs on the ServiceNow server.
A script that runs in the user's web browser to manage the behavior of a form.
A script that manages the connection between the client and the server.
A script used to write and run automated tests.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Scripts that run on the server are Business Rules or Script Includes.
Correct: Client Scripts are JavaScript that execute on the client-side (the browser) to make forms interactive and user-friendly.
Incorrect: This is managed by the platform's underlying architecture.
Incorrect: This is done using the Automated Test Framework (ATF).
questions.explanation: The key to understanding Client Scripts is the word 'client'. They are scripts that are downloaded and executed by the client's web browser. They are used for tasks that need to happen instantly on the form without waiting for a round trip to the server, such as hiding a field, making a field mandatory, or performing simple data validation as the user types.

questions.question: What is the ServiceNow 'Service Portal'?
answers: A back-end interface for system administrators to manage the platform.
A framework for creating a user-friendly, mobile-ready, self-service experience for end-users.
A tool for designing and running automated workflows.
A database that stores all service-related configuration items.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The back-end interface is the standard platform UI.
Correct: The Service Portal provides an alternative, modern user experience, often used as a self-service front-end for employees to request services, search the knowledge base, and get help.
Incorrect: This is Flow Designer.
Incorrect: This is the CMDB.
questions.explanation: The Service Portal is a key part of the ServiceNow user experience. It provides a more modern, web-friendly interface that is separate from the standard back-end UI used by fulfillers. It is highly customizable and is the preferred interface for delivering services and information to end-users who do not need access to the full platform.

questions.question: Which role, in addition to 'admin', is required to modify Access Control Lists (ACLs)?
answers: security_admin
itil_admin
user_admin
acl_manager
feedbacks: Correct: The 'security_admin' role is a special, elevated privilege role that must be explicitly activated to modify ACLs. This is a safety feature to prevent accidental changes to security rules.
Incorrect: The 'itil_admin' role can manage ITSM application settings, but not core platform security like ACLs.
Incorrect: The 'user_admin' role is for managing users and groups.
Incorrect: While this sounds plausible, the correct role name is 'security_admin'.
questions.explanation: To enhance security, ServiceNow requires a user to have the 'admin' role and also to explicitly elevate their privileges to the 'security_admin' role before they can make any changes to Access Control Lists. This acts as a 'safety switch', ensuring that an administrator is consciously making a decision to modify the core security of the platform.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ways to trigger a notification? (Select TWO)
answers: When a record is inserted or updated.
When an event is fired.
When a user logs out.
When a report is viewed.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the most common trigger. A notification can be configured to send when a record on a specific table is created or changed.
Correct: Events can be fired from scripts (like Business Rules or Workflows), providing a flexible way to trigger notifications from anywhere in the platform.
Incorrect: While a script on logout could fire an event, 'user logout' is not a direct trigger for a notification.
Incorrect: Viewing a report does not trigger a notification.
questions.explanation: Notifications can be triggered in two primary ways. The first is directly by a database action: a notification can be configured to run whenever a record is inserted or updated on a specific table and meets certain conditions. The second, more flexible method, is to have the notification be triggered by an 'event'. This allows a script to decide exactly when to fire the event, giving the developer more control over when the notification is sent.

questions.question: What does a 'Reference' field store in the database?
answers: The display value of the referenced record.
The sys_id of the referenced record.
A copy of the entire referenced record.
A URL link to the referenced record.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The display value is looked up for display purposes, but it is not what is stored in the field itself.
Correct: A reference field stores the 32-character globally unique ID (sys_id) of the record it is pointing to.
Incorrect: It only stores the sys_id, not the full record.
Incorrect: It stores the sys_id, which the platform then uses to build a link.
questions.explanation: Although a user sees a human-readable name in a reference field (like a user's name), what is actually stored in that field in the database is the sys_id of the referenced record. This is how ServiceNow maintains the relationship between the two records. The platform then looks up the 'display value' of the referenced record to show it in a user-friendly way on the form.

questions.question: You need to create a form that allows users to request a new mobile phone. The form should have variables for 'Phone Model', 'Color', and 'Storage Size'. What is the best way to create this?
answers: Create a new table with columns for Model, Color, and Storage Size.
Create a new Service Catalog Item.
Create a new UI Page.
Create a new Incident category called 'Mobile Phone Request'.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is overly complex for a simple request and doesn't leverage the request fulfillment engine.
Correct: A Service Catalog Item is the perfect tool for this. You can define the item and then add variables to it to capture the user's choices for model, color, and storage.
Incorrect: A UI Page is for creating a completely custom page and is not necessary for a standard request form.
Incorrect: This is a request, not an incident, and should be handled through the Service Catalog.
questions.explanation: The Service Catalog is designed for these types of requests. An administrator would create a new 'Catalog Item' record. Then, using the 'Variables' related list, they would create the three variables needed to capture the user's choices. Finally, they would attach a flow or workflow to handle the approval and fulfillment process.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a one-to-many relationship in ServiceNow?
answers: A single user can be a member of multiple groups, and a single group can have multiple users.
A single Incident can have multiple Incident Tasks.
A single CI can have only one owner.
A change request can be associated with only one problem.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a many-to-many relationship.
Correct: The Incident is the 'one' and the Incident Tasks are the 'many'. Each Incident Task record has a reference field pointing back to its parent Incident.
Incorrect: This is a one-to-one relationship.
Incorrect: This is a one-to-one relationship.
questions.explanation: A one-to-many relationship exists when one record can be related to many other records. The relationship between an Incident and its associated tasks (Incident Tasks) is a classic example. The parent Incident record is the 'one', and it can have many child Incident Task records associated with it.

questions.question: What is a 'coalesce' field used for in a transform map?
answers: To merge multiple source rows into a single target record during an import.
To make a field on the target table a mandatory field.
To use a source field as a unique key to match and update records in the target table.
To automatically translate the value of a field from one language to another.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Coalescing does not merge rows.
Incorrect: This is done with a data policy or dictionary setting.
Correct: When you coalesce on a field, ServiceNow uses it to see if a record already exists. If it finds a match, it updates the record; if not, it creates a new one.
Incorrect: This is not the function of coalescing.
questions.explanation: Coalescing is the primary mechanism for preventing duplicate records during data imports. By selecting a field to coalesce on (such as an Employee ID for users, or an Asset Tag for CIs), you tell the transform map to use that field as a unique identifier when deciding whether to update an existing record or insert a new one.

questions.question: Which of the following would you use to add a button to the Incident form that, when clicked, automatically resolves the incident and sends a notification?
answers: A UI Policy
A UI Action
A Business Rule
A Client Script
feedbacks: Incorrect: A UI Policy cannot create a button.

Correct: A UI Action is used to create buttons, links, and context menu items. It can contain a script that performs server-side actions like updating the record and firing an event for a notification.
Incorrect: A Business Rule runs automatically on a database action; it cannot create a button that a user clicks.
Incorrect: A client script can respond to a button click, but the UI Action is what creates the button itself.
questions.explanation: UI Actions are designed to add interactive elements to the UI. For this scenario, an administrator would create a new UI Action for the Incident table. They would set the 'Action name' (for scripting), the 'Name' (the text on the button, e.g., 'Resolve Incident'), and then write a server-side script to set the incident's state to 'Resolved' and fire an event to trigger the notification.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid variable types for a Service Catalog item? (Select THREE)
answers: Multiple Choice
Reference
Single Line Text
Business Rule
ACL
Transform Map
feedbacks: Correct: This variable type presents a list of options where the user can select only one (e.g., using radio buttons).
Correct: This variable allows the user to select a record from another table (e.g., selecting a user from the User table).
Correct: This variable provides a simple, single-line text box for input.
Incorrect: A Business Rule is a type of server-side script, not a catalog variable type.
Incorrect: An ACL is a security rule, not a catalog variable type.
Incorrect: A Transform Map is used for data imports, not as a catalog variable.
questions.explanation: The Service Catalog provides a rich set of variable types to build user-friendly request forms. Common types include 'Single Line Text' for short text input, 'Multiple Choice' for presenting a list of options, and 'Reference' for allowing a user to look up and select a record from another table in the system.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of the 'g_user' object in a client script?
answers: To get information about any user in the system by passing their sys_id.
To provide information about the currently logged-in user, such as their name, sys_id, and roles.
To modify user records directly from the client.
To query the entire user table for a list of all active users.
feedbacks: Incorrect: 'g_user' only contains information about the currently logged-in user.
Correct: The g_user object is a client-side object that holds session information about the current user, which can be used by client scripts.
Incorrect: User records must be modified on the server; the g_user object is read-only.
Incorrect: Querying the user table requires a server call (e.g., using GlideAjax). The g_user object does not contain a list of all users.
questions.explanation: The 'g_user' object is a convenient, read-only object available in client-side scripts. It contains key information about the user whose browser is running the script, such as `g_user.userID` (the sys_id), `g_user.userName`, and `g_user.hasRole()`, which is a method to check if the user has a specific role. This avoids the need for a server lookup for basic user information.

questions.question: How can an administrator view the dictionary for a field directly from a form view?
answers: Double-click the field's value.
Right-click the field's label and select 'Configure Dictionary'.
Click the help icon (?) on the form header.
Use the filter navigator to search for the field name.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would typically open the list editor or do nothing.
Correct: This context menu option is a direct shortcut to the system dictionary entry for that specific field.
Incorrect: The help icon provides general form help, not a link to the dictionary.
Incorrect: This would not work and is not the correct procedure.
questions.explanation: This is a common shortcut used by administrators and developers. Instead of navigating through the 'System Definition' menus, you can simply go to a form containing the field you're interested in, right-click on the field's label (not its value), and the context menu will provide a 'Configure Dictionary' option that takes you directly to that field's dictionary record.

questions.question: Which feature is used to define and measure time-based service commitments, such as the time to resolve a P1 incident?
answers: Metrics
A Service Level Agreement (SLA)
A Business Rule
A Key Performance Indicator (KPI)
feedbacks: Incorrect: While a metric can track time, an SLA is the feature specifically designed to define and manage a service commitment.
Correct: SLAs are the standard mechanism for defining time-based targets for tasks and for tracking performance against those targets.
Incorrect: A Business Rule is for automating logic, not for measuring time commitments.
Incorrect: A KPI is a value that measures performance; the SLA is the mechanism that provides the data for many KPIs.
questions.explanation: Service Level Agreements (SLAs) are a core component of IT Service Management. In ServiceNow, an SLA Definition record is used to configure the rules for a service commitment, including the duration, the schedule (e.g., 8-5 business days), and the start, pause, and stop conditions. The system then automatically tracks tasks against these definitions.

questions.question: What is the name of the table that stores the definitions of roles?
answers: sys_user_grmember
sys_user
sys_user_role
sys_security_acl_role
feedbacks: Incorrect: This table links users to groups.
Incorrect: This table stores user records.
Correct: The Role [sys_user_role] table contains the definition for every role in the instance.
Incorrect: This table links ACLs to roles.
questions.explanation: The definitions for all roles in the system—their names, descriptions, and the applications they contain—are stored in the Role [sys_user_role] table. When an administrator creates a new role, they are creating a new record in this table.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'Save' and 'Update' when modifying an existing record?
answers: 'Save' keeps you on the form, while 'Update' saves the record and returns you to the previous list.
'Save' is for administrators, and 'Update' is for ITIL users.
'Save' can be undone, but 'Update' cannot.
There is no difference; the buttons are identical.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the key difference. Both actions save the changes to the database. 'Save' is for when you want to save your progress and continue working on the form. 'Update' is for when you are finished with your changes.
Incorrect: The availability of these buttons is based on permissions, not a specific role difference like this.
Incorrect: Neither can be easily 'undone' without going to the audit history.
Incorrect: They have a distinct and important difference in their navigation behavior after saving.
questions.explanation: When you are editing an existing record, you will often see two UI Actions for saving: 'Save' and 'Update'. They both write the changes to the database. The only difference is what happens next. 'Save' performs the save and reloads the form, keeping you on the same page. 'Update' performs the save and then redirects your browser back to the list or page you came from.

questions.question: You are creating a catalog item and need a variable that will allow the user to select multiple options from a list (e.g., 'Select all the software you need'). What variable type should you use?
answers: Multiple Choice
Select Box
List Collector
Reference
feedbacks: Incorrect: The 'Multiple Choice' variable type only allows a single selection.
Incorrect: A 'Select Box' is a dropdown list that only allows a single selection.

Correct: The 'List Collector' variable type provides a slushbucket interface, allowing the user to select one or more items from a list of available options and move them from a 'source' list to a 'selected' list.
Incorrect: A 'Reference' variable only allows the selection of a single record.
questions.explanation: When you need to allow a user to select multiple items from a list, the 'List Collector' is the appropriate variable type. It displays two side-by-side list boxes, allowing the user to move items from the available list on the left to the selected list on the right. This is commonly used for requesting access to multiple groups or selecting multiple software titles.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about a Business Rule configured to run 'async'?
answers: It runs immediately when the form is saved, before any other rules.
It runs on the client's browser after a delay.
It is placed in a queue to be run by a scheduler in the near future, allowing the system to hand control back to the user immediately.
It can only be used on the Incident table.
feedbacks: Incorrect: An async rule does not run immediately.
Incorrect: Async rules run on the server.

Correct: An 'async' business rule is used for long-running operations that do not need to complete before the user sees the result. The system queues the rule to run in the background, which improves the user's interactive experience.
Incorrect: Async business rules can be used on any table.
questions.explanation: 'Async' Business Rules are a tool for improving system performance and user experience. If you have a task that needs to happen after a record is saved, but it might take a long time (e.g., a complex calculation or an integration call), you can configure the rule to run asynchronously. This means the user doesn't have to wait for the rule to finish before the form reloads, as the work is handled by a background scheduler.

questions.question: Which module would an administrator use to view the logs of inbound and outbound emails for the instance?
answers: System Policy > Notifications
System Diagnostics > Debug Log
System Logs > Emails
Connect > Chat
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is where notifications are configured, but it does not show the email logs.
Incorrect: This shows general system debugging messages, not specifically the email log.
Correct: The 'Emails' module provides a list view of the Email [sys_email] table, which logs every email sent from or received by the instance.
Incorrect: This is for the real-time chat feature.
questions.explanation: The Email [sys_email] table is the authoritative log for all email activity. By navigating to 'System Logs > Emails', an administrator can see a list of every email, its subject, recipients, creation date, and current state (e.g., 'Sent', 'Failed'). This is the first place to look when troubleshooting any issue related to email notifications.

questions.question: A user with the 'itil' role can see 50 incidents in the 'Open' incidents list. A user with only the 'ess' (Employee Self-Service) role can only see 10 incidents in the same list. What is the most likely reason for this difference?
answers: The 'ess' user has a filter applied to their list view.
The 'ess' role has an ACL that restricts them to only seeing incidents they have opened themselves.
The 'itil' user is a member of more groups.
The 'ess' user is using the Service Portal, while the 'itil' user is using the standard UI.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While possible, the difference is more likely due to a fundamental security constraint.

Correct: This is a standard security configuration in ServiceNow. 'itil' users can see all incidents, while self-service users are restricted by a 'query' business rule or ACL to only see their own tickets.
Incorrect: Group membership alone doesn't determine record visibility in this way; it's the ACLs that matter.
Incorrect: The underlying security rules (ACLs) apply to both interfaces.
questions.explanation: This scenario is a classic example of data security in action. ServiceNow uses Access Control Lists (ACLs) and 'query' Business Rules to control which records a user can see in a list. A common configuration is to have a rule that says 'if the user does not have the itil role, then only show them records where the 'caller_id' is the currently logged-in user'. This ensures that end-users can only see their own tickets.

questions.question: What is the 'CMDB'?
answers: A tool for managing IT changes and releases.
A database used to store information about all hardware and software assets, as well as their relationships.
A chat tool used for collaboration between IT teams.
A framework for designing low-code applications.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the Change Management application.
Correct: The Configuration Management Database (CMDB) is a repository of all Configuration Items (CIs) and the relationships between them.
Incorrect: This is Connect Chat.
Incorrect: This is App Engine Studio.
questions.explanation: The Configuration Management Database (CMDB) is a core component of the Now Platform. It is the single source of truth for all configuration items (CIs), which can be anything from a server, to a software application, to a business service. The CMDB is critical for understanding the IT environment and is used by many other applications, like Incident, Problem, and Change Management.

questions.question: You are creating a UI Policy for the Incident form. You check the 'Reverse if false' checkbox. What does this do?
answers: It ensures the UI Policy runs a second time with the opposite logic.
It causes the UI Policy to apply the opposite actions when the condition evaluates to false.
It reverses the order of the UI Policy Actions.
It applies the UI Policy only to users with the 'admin' role.
feedbacks: Incorrect: It doesn't re-run the policy.
Correct: When 'Reverse if false' is checked, if the condition is true, the actions are applied. When the condition becomes false, the system automatically undoes those specific actions.
Incorrect: The order of actions is not affected.
Incorrect: This checkbox has no effect on roles or permissions.
questions.explanation: The 'Reverse if false' checkbox is a convenient feature that saves you from having to write a second, opposite UI Policy. For example, if your policy says 'When State is Resolved, make resolution_notes mandatory', checking 'Reverse if false' means that when the State changes to something else (e.g., 'In Progress'), the system will automatically make the 'resolution_notes' field non-mandatory again.

questions.question: Which of the following would you use to add a new application to the Application Navigator?
answers: System UI > Applications
System Definition > Application Menus
System Properties > My Company
Service Catalog > Maintain Items
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not the correct path.
Correct: The 'Application Menus' module is where an administrator can create or modify the applications that appear in the left-hand navigation pane.
Incorrect: This is for setting company information, not for creating application menus.
Incorrect: This is for creating catalog items, not application menus.
questions.explanation: The applications that a user sees in the Application Navigator are defined as records in the Application Menu [sys_app_application] table. An administrator can create a new application by navigating to 'System Definition > Application Menus' and creating a new record. They can then create Modules (links to lists, forms, etc.) to place inside that application.

questions.question: What is a 'Metric' in ServiceNow primarily used for?
answers: To measure and report on the duration of tasks and states.
To set the color and style of reports and gauges.
To define the business value of a Configuration Item.
To enforce mandatory fields on a form.
feedbacks: Correct: A metric is designed to capture time-based data, such as how long an incident was in the 'In Progress' state or how much time passed between creation and resolution.
Incorrect: This is done with styling properties.
Incorrect: This might be an attribute on a CI, but it is not what a metric is for.
Incorrect: This is the function of a UI Policy or Data Policy.
questions.explanation: Metrics are a key tool for process measurement and reporting. An administrator can define a metric to, for example, 'track the time an incident is assigned to the Service Desk'. The system will then create 'Metric Instance' records that capture the start time, end time, and duration for every incident that meets this condition. This data can then be used to create reports on group performance.

questions.question: When an administrator creates a new table, 'u_custom_app', that is an extension of the Task table, which of the following is true?
answers: The new table will not have any fields until the administrator adds them.
The new table will have all the fields from the Task table, and new fields can be added.
The Task table will now have all the fields from the 'u_custom_app' table.
The new table cannot be used in reports.
feedbacks: Incorrect: It will inherit all the fields from the Task table.
Correct: This is the principle of table extension. The new table starts with all the fields and functionality of the parent (Task) and can be further customized.
Incorrect: Inheritance only works one way, from parent to child.
Incorrect: All tables, including custom ones, can be reported on.
questions.explanation: Table extension is a core concept in the Now Platform that promotes reuse. When you extend a table (like Task), your new table ('u_custom_app') is created with all of the parent's fields (e.g., 'number', 'state', 'priority', 'assignment_group') and functionality already built-in. You can then add new fields that are specific to your custom application.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid client script types? (Select TWO)
answers: onLoad
onSubmit
onBefore
onAsync
feedbacks: Correct: An 'onLoad' client script runs when a form is loaded in the browser.
Correct: An 'onSubmit' client script runs when the user clicks a 'Submit', 'Update', or 'Save' button, but before the data is sent to the server.
Incorrect: 'onBefore' is a timing option for a server-side Business Rule, not a client script type.
Incorrect: 'onAsync' describes a type of Business Rule, not a client script.
questions.explanation: Client Scripts have four types that correspond to different user actions on a form: 'onLoad' (when the form loads), 'onChange' (when a specific field's value changes), 'onSubmit' (when the form is submitted), and 'onCellEdit' (when a cell in a list view is edited).

questions.question: Which feature would you use to provide a simplified, question-and-answer interface that guides an employee through the process of reporting a security breach, which then creates a high-priority security incident record?
answers: An Order Guide
A Record Producer
A Content Item
A Standard Change Template
feedbacks: Incorrect: An Order Guide is for ordering multiple items at once.
Correct: A Record Producer is the perfect tool for this. It provides a simple, user-friendly interface in the catalog that, when submitted, creates a record (like an incident) on a different table.
Incorrect: A content item is for providing information, not for creating a record.
Incorrect: This is for pre-approved, low-risk changes, not for reporting security incidents.
questions.explanation: A Record Producer acts as a user-friendly front-end to a back-end table. For a security incident, you wouldn't want to expose the full, complex security incident form to an end-user. Instead, you create a Record Producer with simple questions like 'What happened?' and 'Where did it happen?'. The answers to these questions are then mapped to the fields on the new security incident record that is created.

questions.question: Which of the following would an administrator use to see real-time, interactive conversations between users that are linked to a specific task record?
answers: Email Logs
Connect Chat
The Audit History
User Presence
feedbacks: Incorrect: Email logs show sent and received emails, not real-time chat.
Correct: Connect Chat provides a real-time messaging interface that can be linked directly to any task record, capturing all conversation history in the record's activity stream.
Incorrect: The audit history shows field changes, not conversations.
Incorrect: User presence shows who is currently viewing a record, but not their conversation.
questions.explanation: Connect Chat is ServiceNow's built-in tool for real-time collaboration. A key feature is the ability to start a conversation from a record (like an incident or change request). This links the chat to the record, and the conversation is automatically logged in the 'Activity' section of the form, ensuring all communication about the task is captured in one place.

questions.question: How does ServiceNow identify a target record when using the 'coalesce' method in a transform map?
answers: It uses the record's sys_id by default.
It checks the field marked for coalescing in the transform map against the corresponding field in the target table to find a match.
It checks all fields in the source row against all fields in the target table for a match.
It creates a new record every time and then runs a script to delete any duplicates.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While the sys_id is the unique key, the coalesce method specifically uses a field that you designate.
Correct: The system takes the value from the source field that you've marked to coalesce and looks for an existing record in the target table with that same value in the corresponding field.
Incorrect: It only checks the specific field(s) that you have marked for coalescing.
Incorrect: Coalescing is designed to prevent the creation of duplicates in the first place.
questions.explanation: The coalesce process is very specific. You, the administrator, choose a field in your source data that should be unique (e.g., an Employee ID or an email address). You then check the 'Coalesce' box for that field's mapping. When the transform runs, for each row, it will query the target table to see if there is already a record where the target field has the same value as the incoming source field.

questions.question: What is a 'UI Policy' primarily used for?
answers: To create a button on a form that executes a script.
To control the behavior of fields on a form, such as making them mandatory or visible, without scripting.
To run a script on the server after a record is saved.
To control who can access a form.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a UI Action.
Correct: UI Policies are the primary low-code/no-code tool for making forms dynamic and responsive to user input.
Incorrect: This is a Business Rule.
Incorrect: This is controlled by Access Control Lists (ACLs).
questions.explanation: UI Policies are a cornerstone of the ServiceNow user experience. They allow an administrator to define simple rules like, 'If the 'State' is 'Closed', make the 'Close notes' field mandatory and visible.' These rules are applied in the user's browser, providing instant feedback and a more intuitive interface.

questions.question: Which application would a user access to find a list of predefined services, such as requesting a new laptop or requesting access to a software application?
answers: The CMDB
Incident Management
The Service Catalog
Change Management
feedbacks: Incorrect: The CMDB stores configuration items, it is not a request portal.
Incorrect: Incident Management is for reporting things that are broken, not for requesting new things.
Correct: The Service Catalog provides a user-friendly, online storefront where users can browse for and request predefined goods and services.
Incorrect: Change Management is for managing changes to IT infrastructure and services.
questions.explanation: The Service Catalog is the primary interface for end-users to request services from IT and other departments. It provides a structured and efficient alternative to unstructured requests via email or phone calls. Each item in the catalog can have its own price, description, and fulfillment process.

questions.question: What is a 'Role' in ServiceNow?
answers: A collection of users.
A collection of permissions.
A specific job title within a company.
A type of task that can be assigned to a user.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a Group.
Correct: A role is a record that contains a set of permissions, which grant access to applications, modules, and data.
Incorrect: While a job title might correspond to a role, the role itself is a ServiceNow record representing permissions.
Incorrect: This is a Task.
questions.explanation: A role is the fundamental unit of permission in ServiceNow. Roles (like 'itil', 'admin', or 'report_user') are collections of access rights. To grant a user permissions, you assign them one or more roles. The best practice is to assign roles to groups, and then add users to the groups.

questions.question: What is a 'Display' Business Rule?
answers: A business rule that runs on the client-side when the form is displayed.
A business rule that runs on the server before the form is sent to the client, and is primarily used to pass data to the client using the g_scratchpad.
A business rule that controls which fields are displayed on the form.
A business rule that can only be used on tables that have a 'Display' value set.
feedbacks: Incorrect: All business rules run on the server.

Correct: A display business rule runs after the data is read from the database but before it is displayed to the user. Its main purpose is to perform server-side queries and then pass information to an onLoad client script via the g_scratchpad object.
Incorrect: This is the function of a UI Policy.
Incorrect: Display business rules can be used on any table.
questions.explanation: Display Business Rules are a special type of rule used to optimize form load times. Instead of having an onLoad client script make a slow server call (e.g., via GlideAjax) to get related information, you use a 'display' business rule to get that information from the server first. The rule then puts the information into the `g_scratchpad`, a special object that is passed to the client, where the onLoad script can then access it instantly without another server round trip.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid relationship types that can be created in the Schema Map?
answers: One to One, One to Many, Many to Many
Parent to Child, Child to Parent
Connects to, Runs on, Depends on
Primary to Foreign, Foreign to Primary
feedbacks: Correct: These are the standard database relationship types that can be modeled and visualized in ServiceNow.
Incorrect: While extension creates a parent-child relationship, these are not the formal names of the relationship types.
Incorrect: These are specific relationship types used in the CMDB between CIs, not the general database relationship types.
Incorrect: These are terms related to database keys, not the name of the relationship types themselves.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow's database supports the same fundamental relationship types as other relational databases. These are 'One-to-One', 'One-to-Many' (the most common, implemented with a reference field), and 'Many-to-Many' (which requires a linking table).

questions.question: Which element of the ServiceNow UI displays a list of applications and the modules they contain?
answers: The Content Frame
The Banner Frame
The Application Navigator
The Service Portal
feedbacks: Incorrect: The Content Frame is where the lists and forms are displayed.
Incorrect: The Banner Frame is the bar at the top with the logo and user menu.
Correct: The Application Navigator is the menu on the left-hand side of the screen that provides the primary means of navigating to different parts of the platform.
Incorrect: The Service Portal is a separate user interface, not an element of the standard platform UI.
questions.explanation: The Application Navigator is the main menu in the standard ServiceNow UI. It is a hierarchical list of 'Applications' (folders) which contain 'Modules' (links that lead to lists, forms, reports, etc.). Users can use the filter at the top to quickly find the application or module they are looking for.

questions.question: Which feature would you use to create a report that joins the Incident [incident] table with the User [sys_user] table to show the caller's department in a list of incidents?
answers: A Transform Map
A Database View
A Metric
A UI Page
feedbacks: Incorrect: A Transform Map is for importing data.
Correct: A Database View is the feature designed to create a logical join between two or more tables for reporting purposes.
Incorrect: A metric is for measuring time.
Incorrect: A UI Page is for creating a custom web page.
questions.explanation: When you need to report on fields from two different but related tables in a single list, a 'Database View' is the tool to use. You would create a view that joins the Incident table and the User table where the 'incident.caller_id' field is equal to the 'sys_user.sys_id'. This allows you to treat the joined data as a single virtual table for reporting.

questions.question: What is a 'workflow' in ServiceNow?
answers: A tool for customizing the look and feel of the user interface.
A repeatable sequence of activities and approvals used to automate a process.
A report that shows the flow of data between tables.
A security rule that controls the flow of access permissions.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is done with branding and UI properties.
Correct: A workflow (or a Flow Designer flow) is a visual representation of a process, showing the sequence of tasks, approvals, notifications, and other activities required to complete it.
Incorrect: This is not the function of a workflow.
Incorrect: This is an ACL.
questions.explanation: Workflows are the process automation engine in ServiceNow. They are used to automate multi-step processes like service catalog fulfillment or change request approvals. A workflow provides a drag-and-drop canvas where an administrator can lay out the sequence of activities, decision points, and notifications that make up a process. Note that Flow Designer is the more modern tool for this.

questions.question: Which of the following would you use to find all configuration items (CIs) that are of the class 'Windows Server' and are located in the 'New York' data center?
answers: A filter on a list view of the CMDB [cmdb_ci] table.
A UI Policy
A Business Rule
The Service Catalog
feedbacks: Correct: A list view filter is the most direct way to query the CMDB for CIs that meet specific attribute criteria.
Incorrect: A UI Policy is for controlling form behavior.
Incorrect: A Business Rule is for automating logic, not for querying data.
Incorrect: The Service Catalog is for requesting services, not for browsing the CMDB.
questions.explanation: The most straightforward way to find a set of records that meet specific criteria is to navigate to a list view of the relevant table (in this case, cmdb_ci or a more specific table like cmdb_ci_win_server) and apply a filter. The filter would have two conditions: '[Class] [is] [Windows Server]' AND '[Location] [is] [New York]'.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'g_scratchpad' object?
answers: To provide a temporary storage area for a user to write personal notes on a form.
To pass information from a server-side script (like a display Business Rule) to a client-side script (like an onLoad Client Script).
To store a history of all scripts that have been run on a form.
To allow a client script to directly query the database.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not the function of the g_scratchpad.

Correct: The g_scratchpad is used to avoid making extra, slow server calls from the client. The server gets the data first, puts it in the scratchpad, and the client script can then access it instantly on form load.
Incorrect: This is not the function of the g_scratchpad.
Incorrect: Client scripts cannot directly query the database; they must use a server call like GlideAjax. The scratchpad is a way to avoid this.
questions.explanation: The `g_scratchpad` is a key optimization tool. It is an empty object that is passed from the server to the client during a form load. A 'display' Business Rule (which runs on the server before the form loads) can add properties to it (e.g., `g_scratchpad.caller_manager = current.caller_id.manager;`). Then, an 'onLoad' Client Script (which runs on the client) can immediately access that information (`var mgr = g_scratchpad.caller_manager;`) without having to make another server call.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ServiceNow report sharing options? (Select THREE)
answers: Publish
Schedule
Export to PDF
Add to Update Set
Assign to User
Link to Problem
feedbacks: Correct: This creates a public URL that anyone can use to view the report.
Correct: This allows the report to be automatically generated and emailed to specific users or groups on a recurring basis.
Correct: A report can be exported to various formats, including PDF, which can then be shared as a file.
Incorrect: Reports are data and configurations that can be in an update set, but this is not a 'sharing' option in the reporting interface.
Incorrect: You cannot 'assign' a report to a user like a task. You share it with them.
Incorrect: You cannot link a report to a problem record in this way.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow provides multiple ways to share report data. You can 'Publish' it for public access, 'Schedule' it for automated email delivery, or 'Export' it to a static file format like PDF or CSV for manual distribution.

questions.question: What is a 'UI Script'?
answers: A server-side script that runs when a UI element is rendered.
A global, client-side script that can be loaded on any page in the platform.
A script that is used to create a new user interface.
A script that is attached to a specific UI Action.
feedbacks: Incorrect: UI Scripts are client-side.
Correct: A UI Script is a way to define JavaScript functions or objects that can be made available globally, for use by other client-side scripts like Client Scripts and UI Policies.
Incorrect: This is too generic. UI Pages or UI Builder are used for this.
Incorrect: The script for a UI Action is contained within the UI Action record itself.
questions.explanation: UI Scripts are used for defining reusable client-side code. If you have a complex JavaScript function that you need to call from multiple different client scripts on different forms, you would define it once in a UI Script. You would then mark the UI Script as 'Global', which makes the function available to all other client-side scripts.

questions.question: Which module allows an administrator to see a list of every single configuration change captured in update sets?
answers: System Update Sets > Retrieved Update Sets
System Update Sets > Local Update Sets
System Update Sets > Customer Updates
System Diagnostics > Upgrade History
feedbacks: Incorrect: This shows a list of update sets that have been retrieved from other instances, not the individual changes.
Incorrect: This shows a list of update set records, not the individual changes within them.
Correct: This module shows a list view of the Customer Update [sys_update_xml] table, which contains a record for every single captured customization.
Incorrect: This shows the history of platform upgrades, not customization updates.
questions.explanation: The Customer Update [sys_update_xml] table is the 'log' of all tracked configuration changes. Every time you save a business rule, modify a form, or create a new role while in an update set, a record is created in this table. The 'Customer Updates' module provides a direct view of this table, which is very useful for finding a specific change or seeing what has been modified recently.

questions.question: Which tool allows you to visually see the relationships between tables, showing parent-child inheritance and reference connections?
answers: The CMDB Query Builder
The Schema Map
Dependency View
The Form Designer
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is for building queries on CI data, not for visualizing table structures.
Correct: The Schema Map is a graphical tool that displays the database schema, showing how tables are interconnected through extensions (parent-child) and reference fields.
Incorrect: Dependency View shows relationships between CI records, not the underlying table structures.
Incorrect: The Form Designer is for laying out fields on a form.
questions.explanation: The Schema Map is a key tool for developers and administrators to understand the data model of the platform. It provides a visual, diagram-like view of the tables, showing which tables extend others and which tables have reference fields pointing to others. This can be very helpful when planning a new application or troubleshooting a data issue.

questions.question: What is the name of the role that allows a user to manage user accounts, groups, and roles?
answers: admin
itil
user_admin
security_admin
feedbacks: Incorrect: While 'admin' can do this, it is not the most specific role for this purpose.
Incorrect: The 'itil' role is for IT support staff, not for user administration.
Correct: The 'user_admin' role is specifically designed to grant permissions for creating and managing users, groups, and role assignments.
Incorrect: This role is for managing high-security settings like ACLs, not for general user administration.
questions.explanation: To follow the principle of least privilege, a user who is responsible for managing user accounts should be granted the 'user_admin' role. This gives them all the necessary permissions to perform their job without granting them the full, system-wide access of the 'admin' role.

questions.question: A user wants to filter a list view to show records created by their own team members. Which filter condition would they use?
answers: [Created by] [is] [My Team]
[Assignment Group] [is] [My Team's Group]
[Created by] [is a member of] [My Group]
[Created by.Department] [is] [My Department]
feedbacks: Incorrect: '[My Team]' is not a valid filter condition operand.
Incorrect: This filters on who the record is assigned to, not who created it.
Incorrect: This is not a valid operator.
Correct: Assuming the team is defined by a department, you can dot-walk from the 'Created by' field to the user's department to filter the list.
questions.explanation: This requires using dot-walking within the filter condition. The 'Created by' field is a reference to the User table. The filter allows you to 'dot-walk' from that reference field to fields on the User table. Therefore, you can build a condition like `Created by.Department is <Your Department Name>` or `Created by.Manager is <Your Manager's Name>` to find records created by your team members.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about a custom table created in the Global scope?
answers: Its name will be prefixed with 'x_'.
Its name will be prefixed with 'u_'.
It cannot be accessed by scoped applications.
It is automatically deleted when the user who created it is made inactive.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The 'x_' prefix is for tables in a scoped application.
Correct: Any custom table created by a user or administrator in the global scope is automatically prefixed with 'u_' to distinguish it from baseline system tables.
Incorrect: It can be accessed by scoped applications if the correct permissions are configured.
Incorrect: Tables are independent of the user who created them.
questions.explanation: This is a fundamental naming convention in ServiceNow. When you create a new table (e.g., 'My Custom Table') and you are working in the 'Global' application scope, the system will automatically save the table with the name 'u_my_custom_table'. This helps to prevent conflicts with ServiceNow's own tables and makes it easy to identify customizations.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ways for a user to provide feedback on a knowledge article? (Select TWO)
answers: Flag the article.
Rate the article with a star rating.
Submit a change request for the article.
Delete the article.
feedbacks: Correct: Users can 'flag' an article to bring it to the attention of the knowledge managers for review if it contains incorrect or unclear information.
Correct: The star rating system provides a quick and easy way for users to give quantitative feedback on the helpfulness of an article.
Incorrect: This is not the standard process for providing feedback on a knowledge article.
Incorrect: Only users with specific permissions (like the knowledge admin) can delete articles.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow's Knowledge Management application provides several built-in mechanisms for user feedback. Users can give a simple star rating to indicate the article's usefulness. If they find a specific issue with the article, they can 'Flag' it, which creates a task for the knowledge team to review the feedback and make corrections.

questions.question: Which of the following would you use to create a new module called 'My Team's Work' that links to a filtered list of tasks assigned to your group?
answers: System UI > Modules
A UI Action
A Business Rule
The Service Portal Designer
feedbacks: Correct: The 'Modules' module (under System Definition or System UI) is where you define the individual links that appear under an Application menu in the navigator.
Incorrect: A UI Action creates a button or link on a form or list, not a module in the navigator.
Incorrect: A Business Rule is a server-side script and cannot create UI elements.
Incorrect: This is for designing Service Portal pages, not for configuring the platform UI's application navigator.
questions.explanation: The Application Navigator is composed of Application Menus and Modules. To add a new link like 'My Team's Work', an administrator would navigate to 'System Definition > Modules' and click 'New'. They would then give it a title, choose the application it should appear under (e.g., 'Self-Service'), set the 'Link Type' to 'List of Records', select the 'Task' table, and create a filter for '[Assignment group] [is one of] [My Groups]'.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid timing options for a Business Rule? (Select THREE)
answers: Before
After
Async
onLoad
onSubmit
onChange
feedbacks: Correct: A 'before' business rule runs before a record is saved to the database.
Correct: An 'after' business rule runs after a record is saved to the database.
Correct: An 'async' business rule is queued to run in the background after a record is saved.
Incorrect: 'onLoad' is a type for a client-side Client Script, not a server-side Business Rule.
Incorrect: 'onSubmit' is a type for a Client Script.
Incorrect: 'onChange' is a type for a Client Script.
questions.explanation: Business Rules are server-side scripts that can be triggered at different points of a database transaction. The main timing options are 'before' (for validation), 'after' (for updating related records), 'async' (for long-running tasks that shouldn't hold up the user), and 'display' (before the record is displayed).

questions.question: Which table contains the definitions for the fields (columns) of all tables in the instance?
answers: Table [sys_db_object]
Dictionary Entry [sys_dictionary]
Field Label [sys_documentation]
Choice [sys_choice]
feedbacks: Incorrect: This table contains the definitions of the tables themselves, not their fields.
Correct: The Dictionary Entry table contains a record for every field on every table, defining its type, label, attributes, and other metadata.
Incorrect: This table stores the translated labels for fields, not their core definitions.
Incorrect: This table stores the options for choice list fields, not the definitions of all fields.
questions.explanation: The System Dictionary is composed of several tables, but the 'Dictionary Entry' [sys_dictionary] table is where the individual columns are defined. When you create a new field on a table, you are creating a new record in the `sys_dictionary` table. This record stores all the properties of that field.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the 'Automated Test Framework (ATF)'?
answers: To automatically fix bugs in custom scripts.
To create and run repeatable, automated tests to confirm that application functionality is working correctly.
To test the performance and load capacity of the instance.
To scan the instance for security vulnerabilities.
feedbacks: Incorrect: ATF identifies failures; it does not fix code.
Correct: ATF is used to automate the testing process, allowing developers to create suites of tests that can be run after changes or upgrades to ensure that functionality has not been broken.
Incorrect: This is a different type of testing, not the primary function of ATF.
Incorrect: This is the function of other tools and security scanners.
questions.explanation: The Automated Test Framework (ATF) is a key tool for ensuring instance quality and stability, especially during upgrades. It allows you to create tests that mimic user actions (e.g., 'Open a new incident form', 'Set these field values', 'Click the submit button', 'Verify that the incident was created'). These tests can then be run automatically to catch any regressions or broken functionality.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of 'dot-walking'?
answers: A visual tool for walking through the steps of a workflow.
A method for accessing fields on related records by traversing through reference fields.
A security feature that prevents users from walking through unauthorized data.
A type of report that shows a walk" through a process."
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not what dot-walking is.

Correct: Dot-walking allows you to get data from a related record without having to write a complex script. For example, in a notification on the Incident table, you can use `${caller_id.manager}` to get the name of the incident caller's manager.
Incorrect: This is a fanciful description.
Incorrect: This is not a type of report.
questions.explanation: Dot-walking is a fundamental skill for any ServiceNow administrator or developer. It provides a simple syntax for retrieving data from a chain of related records. When you have a reference field (like 'caller_id'), you can use a dot to access any field on that referenced record (e.g., `caller_id.department`). You can even chain them together (e.g., `caller_id.department.dept_head`).

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Application Navigator'?
answers: To navigate between different ServiceNow instances (e.g., from Dev to Prod).
To provide a hierarchical menu of links to all applications and modules that a user has access to.
To design the navigation for a custom application.
To search the entire platform for a specific record or keyword.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The navigator is for navigation within a single instance.
Correct: The Application Navigator is the main menu on the left of the standard UI, containing folders (Applications) and links (Modules).
Incorrect: This is not the primary function of the navigator itself.
Incorrect: This is the function of the Global Search bar.
questions.explanation: The Application Navigator is the primary means of navigating the standard ServiceNow UI. It is a collapsible menu on the left side of the screen that is organized into applications and modules. A user's roles determine which applications and modules are visible to them in the navigator.

questions.question: A user wants to filter a list of CIs to show all 'Windows Servers' in either the 'New York' OR 'London' location. Which is the most efficient way to build this filter?
answers: [Class] [is] [Windows Server] AND [Location] [is] [New York] AND [Location] [is] [London]
([Class] [is] [Windows Server] AND [Location] [is] [New York]) OR ([Class] [is] [Windows Server] AND [Location] [is] [London])
[Class] [is] [Windows Server] AND [Location] [is one of] [New York, London]
[Class] [is] [Windows Server] AND [Location] [is not] [Tokyo]
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is an impossible condition; a CI cannot be in two locations at once.
Incorrect: While this works, it is unnecessarily complex.
Correct: The 'is one of' operator is the most efficient way to check for a match against multiple values for the same field.
Incorrect: This would include many other locations besides New York and London.
questions.explanation: The 'is one of' operator is a powerful and efficient tool in the ServiceNow filter builder. Instead of creating multiple 'OR' conditions for the same field, you can use a single 'is one of' condition and provide a comma-separated list of the values you want to match. This makes the filter easier to read and maintain.

questions.question: What is a 'UI Action'?
answers: A server-side script that runs when a form loads.
A client-side script that validates data before a form is submitted.
A configurable button, link, or context menu item that can execute code on either the client or server.
A policy that makes fields on a form read-only or mandatory.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not a UI Action.
Incorrect: This is an onSubmit client script.
Correct: UI Actions are the mechanism for adding custom interactive elements to forms and lists.
Incorrect: This is a UI Policy.
questions.explanation: UI Actions are a key tool for customizing the user experience. They allow an administrator to add a 'button' to a form header, a 'link' in the related links section, or an 'option' to a list's context menu. These actions can then be scripted to perform a wide range of tasks, from simple field updates to complex integrations.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid Service Catalog variable types? (Select TWO)
answers: Checkbox
Lookup Select Box
Business Rule
ACL
feedbacks: Correct: The checkbox variable type allows for a true/false selection.
Correct: This variable type provides a dropdown list of choices that are populated from a specified table.
Incorrect: A Business Rule is a type of script, not a catalog variable.
Incorrect: An ACL is a security rule, not a catalog variable.
questions.explanation: The Service Catalog offers a wide variety of variable types to create user-friendly and powerful request forms. A 'Checkbox' is perfect for simple yes/no questions. A 'Lookup Select Box' is very useful when you want to present the user with a dropdown list of choices that are sourced from a table in the system (e.g., a list of available departments).

questions.question: Which of the following is true about how ACLs are evaluated?
answers: The first rule that matches the object and grants access will be used, and no other rules are evaluated.
All ACLs for an object are evaluated, and the user is granted the highest permission level found.
ACLs are only evaluated when a user opens a form.
Field-level ACLs are always evaluated before table-level ACLs.
feedbacks: Correct: ServiceNow uses an efficient ACL evaluation process. It evaluates rules and the first one that explicitly grants the requested access to the user will be used, and the process stops.
Incorrect: The evaluation stops at the first rule that grants access.
Incorrect: ACLs are evaluated for any database access, including list views, reports, and integrations.
Incorrect: Table-level ACLs are evaluated first. If a user fails the table-level ACL, they are denied access regardless of any field-level rules.
questions.explanation: The ACL evaluation process is designed for efficiency. When a user tries to access a record, the system looks for an ACL rule that matches the object (e.g., the incident table and the read operation). It checks rules from most specific to least specific. As soon as it finds a rule that the user passes (the condition, roles, and script all evaluate to true), it grants access and stops processing any more rules for that object.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'User Criteria' feature in ServiceNow?
answers: To define the criteria for creating a new user account.
To control access to Service Catalog items and Knowledge Base articles.
To set the criteria for a user's password complexity.
To filter the list of users in a reference field.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not the function of User Criteria.
Correct: User Criteria is the primary mechanism for defining who can see and use specific catalog items and knowledge articles, based on the user's roles, groups, department, etc.
Incorrect: This is done through system security properties.
Incorrect: This is done with a reference qualifier.
questions.explanation: User Criteria is a powerful and flexible access control tool for the self-service parts of ServiceNow. Instead of using simple roles, you can create complex criteria like 'Show this item to all users in the Finance department who are located in the US and have the 'manager' role'. This allows for very granular control over who can see what in the Service Catalog and Knowledge Base.

questions.question: What is a 'Data Source' in the context of an import set?
answers: The ServiceNow table that will be the final destination for the imported data.
A record that defines where to get the data to be imported, such as from an attached file or a JDBC connection.
A report that shows the source of all data in a table.
The user who is the source of the data import request.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the 'target table'.
Correct: The Data Source record defines the source of the data, whether it's a file, a connection to another database, or an LDAP directory.
Incorrect: This is not the function of a Data Source.
Incorrect: This is not what a Data Source record represents.
questions.explanation: The first step in any import set process is to define the 'Data Source'. This record tells the system where to find the data. For example, if you are importing from a spreadsheet, you would create a Data Source of type 'File', and then attach your spreadsheet to that data source record.

questions.question: What is a 'dictionary override' used for?
answers: To override the language dictionary for a specific user.
To allow a field on a child table to behave differently than it does on the parent table.
To create a new entry in the System Dictionary.
To override a user's role permissions for a specific field.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not what a dictionary override is for.

Correct: A dictionary override allows you to change the properties (like the default value, mandatory status, or choice list) of an inherited field on a specific child table without affecting the parent.
Incorrect: A dictionary override modifies the behavior of an existing dictionary entry on a specific table.
Incorrect: This is done with an ACL.
questions.explanation: Dictionary overrides are a key tool for working with extended tables. For example, the Incident and Change Request tables both extend the Task table. The Task table has a 'State' field. If you want the choices for 'State' to be different on the Incident form than they are on the Change form, you would use a dictionary override for the 'State' field on each of the child tables.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid components of a filter condition in ServiceNow? (Select THREE)
answers: Field
Operator
Value
Table
Script
Role
feedbacks: Correct: The first part of any condition is the field you want to check (e.g., 'Category').
Correct: The second part is the operator, which defines the comparison (e.g., 'is', 'is not', 'contains').
Correct: The third part is the value you are comparing against (e.g., 'Hardware').
Incorrect: The table is selected before you start building the filter; it is not a component of the condition line itself.
Incorrect: While some advanced filters can use scripts, 'Script' is not one of the three basic components of a standard filter condition.
Incorrect: A role is not a component of a filter condition.
questions.explanation: Every standard filter condition in ServiceNow is made up of three parts, often called a 'triple'. First, you select the 'Field' from the table. Second, you select the 'Operator' for the comparison. Third, you provide the 'Value' to compare the field against. For example: [Priority] [is] [1 - Critical].

questions.question: Which feature allows you to capture a series of configuration changes and move them as a single unit to another instance?
answers: An Import Set
An Update Set
A Transform Map
A Scoped Application
feedbacks: Incorrect: Import Sets are for moving data.
Correct: An Update Set is a container for configuration changes that can be moved between instances.
Incorrect: A Transform Map is part of the Import Set process.
Incorrect: While a scoped application is a container for its own components, an Update Set is the general-purpose tool for moving any set of configuration changes.
questions.explanation: Update Sets are the primary mechanism for promoting customizations through a development lifecycle (e.g., from Dev to Test to Prod). They act as a 'package' of changes that can be easily transported and applied to another instance, ensuring that all related configurations are moved together.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about ACL execution?
answers: If multiple ACLs match, the one with the highest 'Order' value is processed first.
To access a record's field, a user must pass both a table-level ACL and a field-level ACL for that field.
A user only needs to pass one ACL, either at the table or field level, to gain access.
ACL scripts are executed before the role and condition checks.
feedbacks: Incorrect: ACLs are processed from most specific to least specific, not based on an 'Order' field.
Correct: A user must first have access to the record (pass the table ACL) and then have access to the specific field (pass the field ACL).
Incorrect: Both levels of checks must be passed.
Incorrect: The condition and role checks happen first. The script is only evaluated if the condition and roles are met.
questions.explanation: ACLs are evaluated in a hierarchical manner. First, the system checks for access to the table itself (e.g., can the user read records from the 'incident' table?). If that check passes, the system then checks for access to the specific field the user is trying to see (e.g., can the user read the 'short_description' field?). The user must pass both checks to see the data.

questions.question: What is a 'gauge' in ServiceNow?
answers: A tool for measuring the pressure in a server rack.
A widget that can be placed on a homepage or dashboard to display a report or other data summary.
A security mechanism that gauges a user's trust level.
A type of script used for measuring performance.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a fanciful answer.
Correct: A gauge is a visual representation of a report's data that can be added to a homepage or dashboard for at-a-glance viewing.
Incorrect: This is not a ServiceNow feature.
Incorrect: This describes a metric or a performance analytics script.
questions.explanation: Gauges were the original way to build homepages in ServiceNow. A gauge is simply a 'window' on a homepage that displays a report. You could add multiple gauges to a homepage to create a custom dashboard. Note that in modern ServiceNow, 'widgets' on dashboards have largely replaced gauges on homepages.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'glide.product.logo' system property?
answers: To set the main logo image that appears in the banner frame of the UI.
To set the small icon that appears in the browser tab (the favicon).
To set the logo that appears on the system login page.
To set the logo used in all email notifications.
feedbacks: Correct: This property's value should be the filename of the image (uploaded to System UI > Images) that you want to use as the company logo in the top-left corner of the UI.
Incorrect: This is a different property, often named 'glide.product.favicon'.
Incorrect: The login page theme is configured separately.
Incorrect: Email notification templates are configured separately.
questions.explanation: One of the first and most common branding customizations an administrator performs is to replace the default ServiceNow logo with their own company's logo. This is done by first uploading the logo image to the instance and then setting the 'glide.product.logo' system property to the name of that image file.

questions.question: Which ServiceNow tool is used to build and manage automated, multi-step processes that can include approvals, tasks, and notifications?
answers: The CMDB
Flow Designer or Workflow Editor
The Service Catalog
The System Dictionary
feedbacks: Incorrect: The CMDB is a database, not a process automation tool.
Correct: Flow Designer (the modern tool) and the legacy Workflow Editor are the two primary tools for designing and executing automated, multi-step processes.
Incorrect: The Service Catalog is the front-end for requesting services; the flow or workflow is the back-end engine that fulfills them.
Incorrect: The System Dictionary defines the data structure, it does not automate processes.
questions.explanation: When a request or a task needs to go through a repeatable, multi-step process, that process is automated using either a Flow Designer 'flow' or a legacy 'workflow'. These tools provide a visual canvas for laying out the sequence of activities, such as getting a manager's approval, creating a task for a fulfillment group, and sending a notification to the user.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ways to create a 'Favorite' in the standard UI? (Select TWO)
answers: Click the star icon next to a module in the Application Navigator.
Drag a filtered list's breadcrumbs to the Favorites bar.
Send an email to the 'favorites@<instance_name>' email address.
Right-click on a form and select 'Add to Favorites'.
feedbacks: Correct: Clicking the star adds or removes that module from your personal Favorites list.
Correct: This is a quick way to save a specific, filtered view of a list as a one-click favorite.
Incorrect: This functionality does not exist.
Incorrect: This context menu option does not exist on forms by default.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow provides two very convenient ways for users to personalize their navigation with Favorites. For any Application or Module in the navigator, you can simply click the star icon to add it to your Favorites. For a specific, filtered list of records you use often, you can apply the filter and then drag the resulting 'breadcrumbs' to the Favorites bar to save it.

questions.question: Which server-side script object provides access to the fields and values of the record that is currently being processed by a Business Rule?
answers: g_form
g_user
current
g_scratchpad
feedbacks: Incorrect: `g_form` is a client-side object used in Client Scripts to manage the form.
Incorrect: `g_user` is a client-side object that contains information about the logged-in user.
Correct: In a server-side script like a Business Rule, the 'current' object represents the record that triggered the rule, and its properties can be used to read or modify the record's field values.
Incorrect: `g_scratchpad` is an object used to pass information from a display Business Rule to the client.
questions.explanation: The 'current' object is fundamental to server-side scripting in ServiceNow. When a business rule runs on a record (e.g., an incident), the 'current' object holds all the fields of that incident. You can read values (e.g., `var priority = current.priority;`) and you can set values (e.g., `current.short_description = 'New text';`).

questions.question: Which of the following would an administrator use to configure the fields and layout of a form?
answers: The Schema Map
The Form Designer
A Business Rule
A UI Action
feedbacks: Incorrect: The Schema Map is for visualizing table relationships.
Correct: The Form Designer provides a graphical, drag-and-drop interface for arranging fields, sections, and other elements on a form.
Incorrect: A Business Rule is for executing server-side scripts.
Incorrect: A UI Action is for creating buttons and links.
